prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Kansas City. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Kansas City Missouri for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
I can do that — to give you useful, specific practice names I need one quick detail: which part of the Kansas City area are you in or willing to travel to? (Kansas City, MO vs. Kansas City, KS, or a ZIP code, and how far you’ll travel — e.g., 10–30 miles.) Also tell me if you have dental insurance and whether you need a single implant, multiple implants, full-arch work, or grafting/sinus lift — those change which specialists you should see.

While you reply, here’s a plan so you know what I’ll look for and why — plus who to call first and what to ask.

Which kinds of practices to call first (and why)
- Oral surgeons (OMS): best for surgical placement of implants, complex cases, bone grafts/extractions/sinus lifts, IV sedation. Call an OMS if you expect surgery or have medical issues.
- Periodontists: specialists in gums and implants with a strong focus on long-term implant health and implant placement/maintenance.
- Prosthodontists: specialists in designing and restoring implant crowns, bridges, or full-arch prostheses; call them if you want the best aesthetic/function outcome for the visible teeth.
- Implant-focused private practices or multi-specialty implant centers: some practices combine surgery and restoration under one roof — convenient for coordination and often faster timelines.
- University dental clinics (UMKC School of Dentistry): good option if you want lower cost or are comfortable being treated by residents supervised by specialists.

What I’ll look for when picking specific offices
- Board-certified specialists (AAOMS for oral surgeons, American Academy of Periodontology for perio specialists)
- Experience and volume (how many implants placed per year)
- On-site CBCT (3D imaging) and digital planning
- Restorative and surgical coordination (same location or close team)
- Clear pricing/estimates, sedation options, and financing
- Recent patient reviews and before/after cases

What to call and what to ask (phone script)
- “Hi — I need an evaluation for a dental implant. Do you place implants? Do you perform CBCT scans on-site? Do you work with an in-house prosthodontist/restorative dentist for the crown or do you refer out? What are typical costs and payment/financing options? Can you tell me how many implant cases you do per year and whether you handle bone grafting/sinus lifts? Do you accept my insurance [name insurer]? How long is the wait for a consultation?”
- Red flags: no CBCT available, vague answers about experience, unwillingness to explain total process/timeline/costs.

If you give me your ZIP code or the side of KC you prefer, I’ll compile a short list (3–6) of specific oral surgeons, periodontists, prosthodontists, and a university clinic to call — with a recommended order and why I picked each practice.
